title: Grateful Dead Live at Century II Convention Hall on 1972-11-17

ai_review.summary: Crisp soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1972 Wichita show featuring smoking Bird Song, a classic The Other One jam and stellar Keith piano work.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its crystal‑clear mix, excellent instrument separation and overall superb soundboard quality (with only minor pitch/tempo quirks).  Musically the concert shines – the first set rolls strong and the second set delivers a soaring Bird Song, an exploratory The Other One/Truckin' sequence, a beautiful Brokedown Palace and standout moments from Jerry’s scorching Me & My Uncle and Keith’s jazzy piano solos.  Energy stays high throughout despite a few cuts (Jack Straw, Tennessee Jed).

ai_rating.rationale: All reviews are 5‑star, consistently praising both the performance and the high‑quality soundboard source; only minor technical quirks are noted.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with great instrument separation; praised as “high quality” and “better than Dave’s Picks”. Minor issues: slightly sharp pitch for some listeners and a tiny speed increase, plus isolated cuts in Jack Straw.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Solid first set with tight execution and strong vocals; second set builds into exploratory jams, highlighted by a seamless Truckin' → The Other One transition and a mellow Brokedown Palace finale.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone described as beautiful and “scorching” on Me & My Uncle; praised for powerful lead work throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass and vocals receive high marks – “sounds awesome”, sings Box of Rain like the studio version, and delivers a tight rhythm foundation.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s songs are noted as shining, with strong vocal delivery on his numbers.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano work highlighted as brilliant, jazzy, and a key melodic driver during The Other One and other jams.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann (Billy) described as unstoppable in the extended jams, keeping the rhythm tight.
